propositions.text: Applicants are Polish Roma seeking judicial review of RAD decision confirming RPD's refusal of refugee protection.
propositions.quote: The Applicants, Ms. Katarzyna Jaworowska and Mr. Robert Dyszko, are Polish citizens of Roma ethnicity. They seek judicial review of a decision (Decision) of the Refugee Appeal Division (RAD) of the Immigration and Refugee Board of Canada.

propositions.text: RAD confirmed RPD decision that Applicants are neither Convention refugees nor persons in need of protection under IRPA sections 96 and 97.
propositions.quote: The RAD confirmed the decision of the Refugee Protection Division (RPD) that the Applicants were neither Convention refugees nor persons in need of protection pursuant to sections 96 and 97, respectively, of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act, SC 2001, c 27 (IRPA).

propositions.text: Adequacy of state protection was the determinative issue in both RPD and RAD decisions.
propositions.quote: The adequacy of state protection for the Applicants was the determinative issue in both instances.

paragraphs.summary: Court states Applicants are Polish Roma seeking judicial review of RAD decision confirming RPD's refusal of refugee protection; adequacy of state protection was key issue.

propositions.text: Application is brought under subsection 72(1) of the IRPA.
propositions.quote: This application is brought pursuant to subsection 72(1) of the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: Court states application is brought under subsection 72(1) of IRPA.

propositions.text: Application for judicial review will be dismissed.
propositions.quote: For the reasons that follow, the application will be dismissed.

paragraphs.summary: Court states application will be dismissed.

propositions.text: Applicants arrived in Canada on February 7, 2017 and claimed refugee protection on June 5, 2017.
propositions.quote: The Applicants arrived in Canada from Poland on February 7, 2017 and claimed refugee protection on June 5, 2017.

paragraphs.summary: Court states Applicants arrived in Canada Feb 7, 2017 and claimed refugee protection June 5, 2017.

propositions.text: Applicants were frequently harassed by skinheads at local market due to Roma ethnicity; police took no action despite fights and witnesses disappearing.
propositions.quote: They state that they were frequently harassed at the market by skinheads who would damage their merchandise and call them names due to their Roma ethnicity. They also state that there were often fights at the market but, if security or the police were called, potential witnesses would disappear and no action would be taken.

paragraphs.summary: Applicants say they were harassed by skinheads at market due to Roma ethnicity; police took no action despite fights and witnesses disappearing.

propositions.text: Applicants were attacked by skinheads in Lodz in Dec 2014; both hospitalized; Ms. Jaworowska had miscarriage; police took no follow-up action despite report.
propositions.quote: In December 2014, the Applicants were attacked by a group of skinheads in Lodz, Poland, while buying goods for their market stall. Both of the Applicants were hospitalized due to the severity of their injuries. Ms. Jaworowska remained in hospital for seven days and suffered a miscarriage as a result of the incident. Mr. Dyszko was hospitalized for two days. The hospital called the police and Mr. Dyszko gave information regarding the attack to the officers but the police took no follow-up action.

paragraphs.summary: Applicants say they were attacked by skinheads in Lodz in Dec 2014; hospitalized; police took no follow-up action despite report.

propositions.text: Mr. Dyszko believes he received no job offers due to ethnicity; he resumed trading at markets in Kutno.
propositions.quote: Mr. Dyszko attempted to find a job and registered as unemployed with the Polish employment office. The Applicants believe that he received no offers of employment because of his ethnicity. Mr. Dyszko subsequently resumed his work as a trader at various markets in Kutno.

paragraphs.summary: Applicants say Mr. Dyszko received no job offers due to ethnicity and resumed trading at markets in Kutno.

propositions.text: Mr. Dyszko worked briefly in England in 2016; both Applicants worked there for a few months before returning to Poland.
propositions.quote: In January 2016, Mr. Dyszko travelled to England. There, he worked briefly in construction before returning to Poland. Shortly thereafter, both Applicants travelled to England and worked for a few months. They then moved back to Poland.

paragraphs.summary: Applicants say Mr. Dyszko worked briefly in England in 2016; both worked there for months before returning to Poland.

propositions.text: Applicants remained in Poland until 2017 when they departed for Canada.
propositions.quote: The Applicants remained in Poland until 2017 when they departed for Canada.

paragraphs.summary: Court states Applicants remained in Poland until 2017 before departing for Canada.

propositions.text: RPD decision dated August 24, 2017 focused on adequacy of state protection for Applicants in Poland.
propositions.quote: The RPD’s decision is dated August 24, 2017. The RPD panel focused on the issue of whether adequate state protection would be available to the Applicants in Poland.

propositions.text: RPD considered Prior RPD Decision granting refugee status to Roma claimant from Poland but disagreed with counsel's findings on state protection.
propositions.quote: The panel began by stating that it had assessed all the information presented to it, including a recent decision by another RPD panel (Prior RPD Decision) that related to a Roma refugee claimant from Poland who was granted convention refugee status. The RPD stated: To summarize Counsel’s submission: the Roma face discrimination in all facets of their lives. The claimants, in a forward-looking manner, would not get protection from the police. The panel read the [Prior RPD Decision] but finds it does not agree with counsel’s findings as it relates to state protection.

propositions.text: Each case is decided on its own facts; not every Roma in Poland experiences persecution; cites Varga v Canada and Banya v Canada.
propositions.quote: The panel finds that each case is decided on a case-by-case review and consideration of the facts presented. The information in each claim is dependent upon the personal circumstances of the claimant. The panel finds that not every Roma in Poland has experienced what amounts to persecution. The panel agrees with Justice Harrington as stated in Varga v Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration), 2014 FC 510 [Varga] at paragraph 20: Each case turns on the particular history of the claimant, the record, the adequacy of the analysis by the Tribunal and, indeed, the appreciation of that evidence by various judges of this Court: Banya v Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration), 2011 FC 313, [2011] FCJ No 393 (QL), at para 4.

paragraphs.summary: RPD decision dated Aug 24, 2017 focused on state protection adequacy; disagreed with prior RPD decision; each case decided on facts; cites Varga and Banya.

propositions.text: States presumed capable of protecting citizens absent complete breakdown; claimant bears onus to prove inadequacy of protection on balance of probabilities.
propositions.quote: The RPD noted that, in the absence of complete breakdown, states are presumed to be capable of protecting their citizens. Further, a claimant who alleges inadequate state protection bears the onus of establishing, on a balance of probabilities, the inadequacy of the available protection.

propositions.text: Poland is a democracy with functioning security and judicial processes; burden on Applicants to show inadequate protection was significant.
propositions.quote: As Poland is a democracy with functioning security and judicial processes, the burden placed on the Applicants to demonstrate the inadequacy of state protection was significant.

paragraphs.summary: RPD found states presumed capable of protection absent breakdown; Applicants bore significant burden to prove inadequate protection in Poland.

propositions.text: RPD acknowledged Roma face discrimination but found Polish government making serious efforts to combat violence and discrimination against Roma.
propositions.quote: The panel acknowledged that the Roma as a population in Poland face discrimination. However, it concluded that the documentary evidence showed that the Polish government was making serious efforts in policy and at the operational level to combat violence and discrimination against its Roma population.

paragraphs.summary: RPD acknowledged Roma discrimination but found Polish government making serious efforts to combat it.

propositions.text: Police were called by hospital after December 2014 attack; police did not pursue case due to lack of witnesses, not inaction.
propositions.quote: With respect to the Applicants’ claim, the RPD stated that the police were called when they were hospitalized in December 2014 but that the call was made by hospital officials and not the Applicants. The fact that the police did not pursue the case was a function of the lack of witnesses and not police inaction.

propositions.text: Mr. Dyszko testified he feared retaliation and could not approach higher authorities for redress.
propositions.quote: When questioned why he had not pursued redress, Mr. Dyszko testified that he could not approach the higher levels of state authorities because he feared retaliation.

propositions.text: RPD found Applicants did not utilize available recourses; no denial of protection but reluctance to seek it.
propositions.quote: However, the RPD concluded that there were recourses available to the Applicants that they did not utilize. Although the panel did not question the December 2014 assault, it did not agree that the police were unwilling to aid the Applicants. There was no denial of protection; rather there was reluctance on the part of the Applicants to seek protection.

paragraphs.summary: RPD found police called by hospital after 2014 attack but did not pursue due to lack of witnesses; Applicants feared retaliation but did not seek available recourses.

propositions.text: RPD reviewed documentary evidence and availability of assistance to Roma in Poland, including government and EU funded organizations.
propositions.quote: The RPD reviewed in detail the documentary evidence before it and the availability of assistance to Roma individuals in Poland. The panel referred to the Applicants’ limited education but noted a number of Roma organizations funded by both the Polish government and the European Union were available to assist them.

propositions.text: RPD noted government actions to address discrimination and arrests made in attacks on Roma population.
propositions.quote: The panel also set out the actions taken by the government to address discrimination and the arrests made by police in cases involving attacks on the Roma population.

propositions.text: Claimant alleging subjective fear must take reasonable steps to access protective services absent compelling justification; Applicants failed to do so regarding police.
propositions.quote: Even where the protective services of the home state have gaps or deficiencies, a claimant who alleges a subjective fear must, in the absence of a compelling justification, take reasonable steps to access those services. The claimants have failed to demonstrate they have taken reasonable steps to access any services as it relates to the police.

paragraphs.summary: RPD reviewed evidence of assistance to Roma and government actions; held claimants must take reasonable steps to access protection; Applicants failed to do so.

propositions.text: RPD acknowledged high Roma unemployment but noted government funding for education, healthcare, employment, and no evidence Applicants could not return home.
propositions.quote: With respect to the Applicants’ claims of discrimination due to their Roma ethnicity, the RPD acknowledged that there is a high level of Roma unemployment in Poland but noted that the government has funded education, healthcare, employment and better living conditions for Roma. Further, there was no evidence before the RPD that the Applicants could not return to Poland to the home they had shared with Mr. Dyszko’s grandfather.

paragraphs.summary: RPD acknowledged Roma unemployment but noted government support and no evidence Applicants could not return home.

propositions.text: Applicants allege RPD erred by failing to articulate credibility and factual findings for state protection analysis.
propositions.quote: 1. The RPD erred in failing to enunciate credibility and factual findings as a basis for its state protection analysis;

propositions.text: Applicants allege RPD erred by conducting state protection analysis in factual vacuum.
propositions.quote: 2. The RPD erred by conducting its state protection analysis in a factual vacuum;

propositions.text: Applicants allege RPD erred by relying on selective, general and dated country condition evidence.
propositions.quote: 3. The RPD erred by relying on selective, general and dated country condition evidence;

propositions.text: Applicants allege RPD erred by failing to mention and properly consider Applicants’ country documents.
propositions.quote: 4. The RPD erred by failing to mention and properly consider the Applicants’ country documents;

propositions.text: Applicants allege RPD erred by failing to explain why it reached different conclusion than Prior RPD Decision on same country evidence.
propositions.quote: 5. The RPD erred by failing to clearly articulate reasons why its analysis of the same country condition evidence led to a different conclusion from that of the Prior RPD Decision.

paragraphs.summary: Applicants allege RPD erred in credibility findings, factual vacuum, selective evidence, ignoring their documents, and failing to explain differing conclusion from prior RPD decision.

propositions.text: RAD reviewed record independently and found RPD correctly concluded Applicants failed to rebut presumption of state protection.
propositions.quote: The RAD reviewed the record independently and found that the RPD had correctly concluded that the Applicants had failed to rebut the presumption of state protection.

paragraphs.summary: RAD independently reviewed record and found RPD correctly concluded Applicants failed to rebut presumption of state protection.

propositions.text: Onus is on Applicants to rebut presumption of adequate state protection with clear and convincing evidence of state's inability to protect.
propositions.quote: The RAD stated that the onus was on the Applicants to rebut the presumption of adequate state protection. In order to do so, they were required to provide clear and convincing evidence of the Polish state’s inability to protect them.

propositions.text: Claimant must provide information on steps taken to obtain protection; mere police inaction insufficient.
propositions.quote: The panel noted that it was not sufficient for a claimant to go to the police and say the police did nothing. The RAD emphasized that “the appellants must provide information as to what steps they took to obtain protection”.

paragraphs.summary: RAD stated Applicants must rebut presumption with clear evidence of state's inability and show steps taken to obtain protection; mere police inaction insufficient.

propositions.text: RAD found RPD gave clear reasons why Applicants failed to rebut presumption of state protection.
propositions.quote: The RAD found that the RPD provided clear and specific reasons as to why the Applicants had not rebutted the presumption of state protection.

propositions.text: RAD reviewed RPD's consideration of 2014 incident and Applicants' failure to report or follow up after police called by hospital.
propositions.quote: The panel reviewed the RPD’s consideration of the December 2014 incident and the Applicants’ failure to either report the incident or to follow up once the police had been called by the hospital.

propositions.text: Claimant must take reasonable steps to access protective services or provide compelling reasons for not doing so; subjective fear insufficient.
propositions.quote: The RAD stated that even where there may be gaps or deficiencies in a state’s protection, a refugee claimant cannot merely allege a subjective fear but must take reasonable steps to access the available services or provide compelling reasons for not doing so.

propositions.text: RAD concluded RPD did not err in finding Applicants' reasons for not seeking protection did not show failure of state protection.
propositions.quote: The RAD concluded that the RPD did not err in finding that the Applicants’ responses about why they did not seek protection in Poland did not evidence a failure of state protection.

paragraphs.summary: RAD found RPD gave clear reasons Applicants failed to rebut presumption; Applicants did not report or follow up 2014 incident; must take reasonable steps or justify not doing so; RPD did not err.

propositions.text: RAD found RPD properly weighed current National Documentation Package over Applicants' dated, general country documents.
propositions.quote: The RAD then addressed the Applicants’ allegation that the RPD had failed to adequately consider their country documentation. The RAD reviewed the available documentation and found that the RPD panel made no error in giving greater weight to the current objective and comprehensive information from March 2017 in the National Documentation Package (NDP) than to the Applicants’ dated and general country documents.

propositions.text: RAD independently reviewed country documents and agreed with RPD that evidence did not rebut presumption of state protection in Poland.
propositions.quote: The RAD also independently reviewed the available country documentation and agreed with the RPD’s conclusion that the objective evidence did not rebut the presumption of state protection in Poland.

paragraphs.summary: RAD found RPD properly weighed current documentation over Applicants' dated documents and agreed evidence did not rebut presumption of state protection.

propositions.text: The RPD considered Applicants' circumstances and concluded they failed to rebut presumption of adequate state protection.
propositions.quote: The RPD demonstrated that it not only considered the current, objective country conditions, but also proceeded to analyze the appellants’ particular circumstances and failure to seek protection, and properly concluded that the appellants had not provided clear and convincing evidence to rebut the presumption of adequate state protection.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD found the RPD considered Applicants' circumstances and concluded they failed to rebut presumption of adequate state protection.

propositions.text: The RAD independently analyzed country documents and found Polish government made serious efforts to protect Roma.
propositions.quote: The RAD also independently analyzed the country documentation, concluding that Roma in Poland face serious challenges but that the government had “made serious efforts, with concrete results, to provide protection to the Roma”.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD independently analyzed country documents and found Polish government made serious efforts to protect Roma.

propositions.text: One RPD panel need not follow another; this RPD panel gave clear reasons for its state protection analysis.
propositions.quote: One panel of the RPD is not obligated to follow the reasoning or factual findings of another; here, the RPD provided clear and specific reasons for its own state protection analysis based upon the particular history of these appellants.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD found one RPD panel need not follow another; this panel gave clear reasons for its state protection analysis.

propositions.text: Did the RAD apply the incorrect test for adequate state protection?
propositions.quote: Did the RAD apply the incorrect test for adequate state protection?

propositions.text: Was the RAD’s conclusion that adequate state protection would be available to the Applicants reasonable?
propositions.quote: Was the RAD’s conclusion that adequate state protection would be available to the Applicants reasonable?

paragraphs.summary: Applicants raise two issues: whether RAD applied incorrect test and whether RAD's conclusion on state protection was reasonable.

propositions.text: Whether RAD applied wrong test is reviewed for correctness; application of test reviewed for reasonableness.
propositions.quote: The question of whether the RAD applied the wrong test for adequate state protection is reviewed by this Court for correctness while its application of the test to the facts of the case is reviewed against the standard of reasonableness

paragraphs.summary: Court states review standard: correctness for test applied, reasonableness for application to facts.

propositions.text: Reasonableness review requires deference; court interferes only if RAD's conclusion lacks justification or is outside acceptable outcomes.
propositions.quote: This Court will only interfere if the RAD’s conclusion regarding the availability of adequate state protection to the Applicants in Poland lacks justification, transparency, or intelligibility, and falls outside the range of possible, acceptable outcomes

paragraphs.summary: Court explains reasonableness standard requires deference and interference only if RAD's conclusion lacks justification or is unreasonable.

propositions.text: Applicants submit RAD and RPD erred in applying proper state protection test, citing RPD excerpts showing misapplication.
propositions.quote: The Applicants submit that both the RAD and the RPD erred in applying the proper state protection test. The Applicants cite a number of excerpts from the RPD decision which they allege demonstrate that the RPD panel may have identified the correct test but misapplied it to their circumstances.

paragraphs.summary: Applicants argue RAD and RPD erred in applying state protection test, citing RPD excerpts showing misapplication.

propositions.text: Both RAD and RPD correctly identified and applied the state protection test; Applicants' submissions better address reasonableness of RAD's decision.
propositions.quote: I find that both the RAD and the RPD correctly identified and applied the test for adequate state protection... Applicants’ submissions... are better considered as submissions questioning the reasonableness of the RAD’s Decision.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds RAD and RPD correctly applied test; Applicants' arguments better address reasonableness of RAD's decision.

propositions.text: Applicants submit RAD's decision unreasonable for three reasons: ignoring factual basis, failing to address operational aspects, and not explaining conclusion against prior RPD decision.
propositions.quote: The Applicants submit that that the Decision was unreasonable for three reasons: 1. The RAD’s analysis of the RPD’s decision ignored the factual basis... 2. The RAD failed to address the operational aspects... 3. The RAD and the RPD did not explain their conclusion...

paragraphs.summary: Applicants submit RAD's decision unreasonable for ignoring facts, failing to address operational aspects, and not explaining conclusion.

propositions.text: Court will consider first two submissions together and then address third regarding prior RPD decision.
propositions.quote: I will consider the Applicants’ first two submissions together... I will then address the third submission regarding the Prior RPD Decision.

paragraphs.summary: Court will consider first two submissions together, then address third regarding prior RPD decision.

propositions.text: Applicants submit RAD and RPD assessed state protection in factual vacuum, focusing only on December 2014 attack and hospital calling police.
propositions.quote: The Applicants submit that the RAD and RPD assessed the adequacy of state protection in a factual vacuum... focusing solely on the December 2014 attack that resulted in their hospitalization.

propositions.text: Applicants argue panels unduly relied on hospital personnel calling police and failed to address their explanation for not following up with police.
propositions.quote: The Applicants also submit that both panels unduly relied on the fact that it was hospital personnel who called the police in December 2014... the RAD and RPD erred in not addressing the Applicants’ explanation for their failure to follow up with the police.

propositions.text: Applicants submit RAD did not assess operational effectiveness of Polish state protection against their circumstances.
propositions.quote: Finally, the Applicants submit that the RAD did not assess the operational effectiveness of the Polish state protection apparatus against their specific circumstances.

paragraphs.summary: Applicants argue RAD and RPD assessed state protection in factual vacuum, unduly relied on hospital calling police, and failed to assess operational effectiveness.

propositions.text: Respondent submits RAD considered Applicants' submission about factual vacuum and gave clear reasons for presumption of state protection.
propositions.quote: The Respondent submits that the RAD specifically considered the Applicants’ submission that the RPD made its decision in a factual vacuum... gave clear and specific reasons as to why they failed to rebut the presumption of state protection.

propositions.text: Respondent submits panels did not err by describing only some incidents and correctly stated burden on Applicants to seek protection.
propositions.quote: The Respondent submits that the panels did not commit a reviewable error by describing only some of the incidents... the RAD correctly stated that it was the Applicants’ burden to demonstrate that they took all reasonable measures to seek protection.

paragraphs.summary: Respondent submits RAD considered factual vacuum claim, gave clear reasons, did not err by describing some incidents, and correctly stated Applicants' burden.

propositions.text: Court finds RAD did not assess state protection in factual vacuum; RAD's analysis of Applicants' failure to engage police was reasonable overall.
propositions.quote: I find that the RAD did not assess the availability of state protection for the Applicants in a factual vacuum... I find that the RAD’s analysis of the Applicants’ failure to engage with Polish authorities was reasonable when considered in its entirety.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds RAD did not assess state protection in factual vacuum and its analysis of Applicants' failure to engage police was reasonable overall.

propositions.text: RAD disagreed with Applicants' argument that RPD erred by basing analysis in factual vacuum, noting RPD considered Applicants' circumstances.
propositions.quote: The RAD further does not agree with the appellants’ argument the RPD erred by basing its state protection analysis in a “factual vacuum”. In its reasons for decision, the RPD clearly demonstrated that it considered the appellants’ particular circumstances...

paragraphs.summary: RAD disagreed with Applicants' argument that RPD erred by basing analysis in factual vacuum, noting RPD considered Applicants' circumstances.

propositions.text: Applicants say factual vacuum means RPD and RAD did not consider reasons for not seeking police protection.
propositions.quote: The Applicants state that the factual vacuum to which they refer is the fact that neither the RPD nor the RAD considered the reasons for which they did not seek police protection in Poland.

propositions.text: Court finds RAD and RPD considered Applicants' explanation for not seeking police protection but found it did not rebut presumption of state protection.
propositions.quote: it is clear in the Decision and in the RPD’s decision that the two panels did consider the Applicants’ explanation but found that it did not rebut the presumption of state protection.

propositions.text: RPD noted hospital called police, Applicants fearful and did not follow up, case closed due to no witnesses, not police shortcoming but fear of retaliation.
propositions.quote: The panel notes that the police were called when the claimants were hospitalized... The panel does not find this nor the fact that no one came forth due to the claimants’ ethnicity as a shortcoming of the police, it appears it was the fear of retaliation.

paragraphs.summary: Applicants say RAD and RPD did not consider reasons for not seeking police; court finds panels considered explanation but found it insufficient to rebut presumption.

propositions.text: RPD addressed why Applicants did not seek higher authorities; Applicants feared retaliation and lacked education; RAD found no error in RPD's analysis.
propositions.quote: The RAD emphasized the RPD’s statements that... a “refugee claimant who alleges a subjective fear must... take reasonable steps to access those services”. The RAD concluded... finds no error in the RPD’s analysis or finding.

paragraphs.summary: RPD addressed Applicants' fear and lack of education for not seeking higher authorities; RAD found no error in RPD's analysis.

propositions.text: Although RAD's consideration of Applicants' explanation was brief, it reflected the evidence before it.
propositions.quote: Although the RAD panel’s consideration of the Applicants’ explanation for their reticence to go to the police was brief, it was reflective of the evidence before it.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds RAD's brief consideration of Applicants' explanation reflected the evidence before it.

propositions.text: Applicants submit RAD failed to consider other discriminatory and violent incidents in their narrative, including market fights and police inaction.
propositions.quote: The Applicants submit that the RAD failed to consider the other discriminatory and violent incidents referred to in their narrative... The Applicants state that market security would not take action and... police would accuse the Applicants of calling them for no reason.

paragraphs.summary: Applicants submit RAD failed to consider other discriminatory and violent incidents including market fights and police inaction.

propositions.text: Applicants' references to market fights were general; no clear evidence of police involvement; only December 2014 attack described in detail; RAD did not err relying on it.
propositions.quote: The Applicants’ references to fights in the market were general in nature... The only incident described in detail by the Applicants is the December 2014 attack. In light of the lack of information... I find that the RAD did not err in basing its state protection analysis on the December 2014 attack.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds Applicants' market fight references general and only December 2014 attack detailed; RAD did not err relying on it.

propositions.text: Applicants submit RAD failed to assess operational adequacy of state protection for Roma in Poland.
propositions.quote: The Applicants also submit that the RAD failed to assess the operational adequacy of state protection for Roma in Poland...

propositions.text: RPD reviewed operational elements of protections for Roma; RAD considered RPD's analysis and Applicants' circumstances.
propositions.quote: The RPD undertook an extensive review of the operational elements of the protections and resources available to the Roma population in Poland. The RAD considered the RPD’s analysis...

paragraphs.summary: Applicants submit RAD failed to assess operational adequacy; court finds RPD reviewed protections and RAD considered that analysis and Applicants' circumstances.

propositions.text: RAD assessed documentary evidence on Roma treatment in Poland, considered Applicants' evidence on 2014 attack and reasons for no police protection sought
propositions.quote: The RAD also conducted its own assessment of the documentary evidence regarding the treatment of the Roma population in Poland. The panel considered the Applicants’ evidence relating to the December 2014 attack and the reasons they provided for why they did not seek police protection or action.

propositions.text: RAD referred to Applicants' background and noted Polish government efforts and results in protection as confirmed by documentary evidence
propositions.quote: The RAD referred to the Applicants’ background, employment history, education and living arrangements in Poland. The RAD noted both the efforts of the Polish government to provide protection and the concrete results of those efforts as confirmed in the documentary evidence.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD assessed documentary evidence and Applicants' background, noting Polish government efforts and results in protecting Roma in Poland.

propositions.text: RAD did not decide in a factual vacuum; its consideration of evidence was transparent and intelligible
propositions.quote: In my view, the RAD did not make its Decision in a factual vacuum. Its consideration of the documentary evidence for Poland and the Applicants’ narrative and evidence was transparent and intelligible.

propositions.text: RAD concluded Applicants failed to rebut presumption of adequate state protection due to lack of clear evidence of attempts to involve police beyond hospital statement
propositions.quote: Its conclusion regarding the Applicants’ failure to rebut the presumption of adequate state protection was based on the lack of clear and convincing evidence of attempts to involve the police or other authorities outside of the statement Mr. Dyszko gave to police in the hospital.

propositions.text: RAD reasonably assessed weight of hospital statement against other recourses and denial of appeal was within possible outcomes
propositions.quote: The RAD’s assessment of the weight of this statement against the additional recourses available to the Applicants was reasonable and its denial of the Applicants’ appeal was within the possible outcomes for the case.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the RAD's decision was transparent, reasonably assessed evidence, and denial of appeal was within possible outcomes.

propositions.text: Applicants argue RAD and RPD did not adequately explain differing state protection analyses and conclusions from Prior RPD Decision
propositions.quote: the Applicants submit that the RAD and RPD panels did not adequately explain why their state protection analyses and conclusions differed from those of the Prior RPD Decision.

propositions.text: Applicants argue RAD could not reasonably reach opposite conclusion on state protection adequacy based on same country evidence
propositions.quote: They argue that the RAD could not reasonably come to an opposite conclusion regarding the adequacy of state protection in Poland for Roma based on the same objective country evidence.

propositions.text: Applicants emphasize they do not contest possibility of different conclusions but focus on general finding in Prior RPD Decision that state protection is unavailable to Roma
propositions.quote: Counsel for the Applicants emphasized that they are not contesting the fact that the RPD and RAD could come to a different conclusion based on the facts before them; their focus is on the general finding in the Prior RPD Decision that state protection is not available to the Roma population in Poland.

propositions.text: Applicants argue for consistency among RPD and RAD panels
propositions.quote: They position the argument as one of requiring consistency among RPD and RAD panels.

paragraphs.summary: Applicants argue RAD and RPD failed to explain differing state protection conclusions from Prior RPD Decision and seek consistency among panels.

propositions.text: Court acknowledges distinction between general state protection finding and application to particular facts
propositions.quote: I acknowledge the distinction drawn by the Applicants between a general finding as to state protection and the application by a decision-maker of the test for adequate state protection to the facts in a particular case.

propositions.text: Court finds RAD made no reviewable error in its treatment of Prior RPD Decision
propositions.quote: However, I find that the RAD made no reviewable error in its treatment of the Prior RPD Decision.

paragraphs.summary: Court acknowledges distinction between general and case-specific state protection findings and finds no error in RAD's treatment of Prior RPD Decision.

propositions.text: Adequacy of state protection is highly fact dependent and linked to claimant circumstances and access to state resources
propositions.quote: The adequacy of state protection is in each case highly fact dependent. Almost inevitably, the adequacy of protection in a country is linked to the circumstances of the particular claimant(s) before a decision-maker and their ability to access state resources.

propositions.text: Finding of no adequate state protection in one case is not determinative for others in same group
propositions.quote: Generally, a finding that adequate state protection is not available to a claimant in one case is not determinative of the adequacy of that protection to other claimants who belong to the same group or segment of a country’s population.

propositions.text: State protection analysis requires assessing state nature, operational effectiveness for group, and claimants' ability to access protection
propositions.quote: A decision-maker is required to begin its analysis with an assessment of the nature of the state in question and its security and judicial processes; to then assess the operational effectiveness of those processes in the context of an identified group to which the claimants belong; and to analyse the ability and actions of the particular claimants in accessing the available state protection.

paragraphs.summary: Court states adequacy of state protection depends on claimant circumstances and requires multi-step analysis of state and claimant factors.

propositions.text: Applicants rely on Siddiqui case to support argument on consistency of findings
propositions.quote: The Applicants rely on the case of Siddiqui v Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration), 2007 FC 6 (Siddiqui) in support of their argument.

propositions.text: Siddiqui involved two RPD panels addressing same terrorism question with same evidence and timeframe
propositions.quote: In Siddiqui, two RPD panels had addressed the same question: whether a division of the Mohajir Quomi Movement (MQM) was engaged in terrorism. The finding in each case was based solely on documentary evidence.

propositions.text: Second RPD panel in Siddiqui made no reference to contradictory findings of first panel despite identical evidence and issue
propositions.quote: In Siddiqui, the second of the two cases, the RPD made no reference to the contradictory findings of the other panel.

propositions.text: Justice Phelan stated failure to explain differing conclusions undermines Board decision integrity and creates aura of arbitrariness
propositions.quote: Justice Phelan stated that its “failure to explain the basis for the different conclusion undermines the integrity of Board decisions and gives them an aura of arbitrariness which is no doubt not intended nor is it acceptable” (Siddiqui at para 19).

paragraphs.summary: Applicants rely on Siddiqui where failure to explain differing findings on identical evidence undermined Board integrity, per Justice Phelan.

propositions.text: Siddiqui finding was discrete, objective, not based on particular claimant facts unlike state protection findings
propositions.quote: In my opinion, the finding regarding MQM in Siddiqui was a discrete, objective determination that was not based on the particular facts before either of the RPD panels.

propositions.text: State protection findings are linked to claimant circumstances except in exceptional country conditions
propositions.quote: As stated above, a state protection finding is necessarily linked to the circumstances of the claimants in question other than in cases involving exceptional country conditions.

paragraphs.summary: Court distinguishes Siddiqui's objective finding from fact-dependent state protection findings linked to claimant circumstances.

propositions.text: Respondent cites Mendoza case illustrating narrow circumstances where arbitrariness concern arises in state protection decisions
propositions.quote: The Respondent cites the case of Mendoza v Canada (Citizenship and Immigration), 2015 FC 251 (Mendoza), as an example of the narrow circumstances in which the concern regarding arbitrariness is present in state protection decisions.

propositions.text: Mendoza court held RPD must explain differing results in claims by family members under similar circumstances
propositions.quote: This court has held that it is incumbent on the RPD Member when reaching a different result than was previously reached by another Member regarding a claim by a family member under similar circumstances, to explain why a contrary result was reached: Mengesha v Canada ... and Siddiqui ...

paragraphs.summary: Respondent cites Mendoza where court requires RPD to explain differing results in similar family member claims to avoid arbitrariness.

propositions.text: Justice Zinn in Mendoza stated differing conclusion undermined RPD decision integrity and created aura of arbitrariness
propositions.quote: Justice Zinn then referred to Siddiqui and stated that the different conclusion in the case before him undermined the integrity of the RPD’s decisions and gave rise to the aura of arbitrariness.

paragraphs.summary: Justice Zinn in Mendoza stated differing conclusions undermined RPD integrity and created arbitrariness aura.

propositions.text: No factual overlap between Applicants and claimants in Prior RPD Decision
propositions.quote: In the present case, there is no factual overlap between the Applicants’ circumstances and those of the claimants in the Prior RPD Decision.

propositions.text: Prior RPD panel did not conduct comprehensive documentary review; conclusion based on particular claimants' experiences
propositions.quote: In addition, I note that the panel in the Prior RPD Decision did not conduct a comprehensive review of the available documentary evidence for Poland. The panel’s conclusion was based on the experiences of the particular claimants.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds no factual overlap with Prior RPD claimants and notes Prior RPD panel's limited documentary review.

propositions.text: RAD did not err in analyzing Applicants' circumstances against country documentation on Roma treatment
propositions.quote: I find that the RAD did not err in conducting its own analysis of the Applicants’ circumstances against the objective country documentation regarding the treatment of Roma in Poland.

propositions.text: RAD addressed Prior RPD Decision and reliance on Varga case, stating panels not required to follow others' reasoning or findings
propositions.quote: In the Decision, the RAD addressed the Prior RPD Decision and the RPD panel’s reliance on Varga v Canada ... The RAD stated that one RPD panel is not required to follow the reasoning or factual findings of another.

propositions.text: RAD noted Prior RPD provided clear reasons based on appellants' particular history
propositions.quote: As the RAD noted, “the RPD provided clear and specific reasons for its own state protection analysis based upon the particular history of these appellants”.

propositions.text: Absent factual overlap, adequacy of state protection must be assessed case-by-case based on facts and country documentation
propositions.quote: Absent the type of factual overlap identified by Justice Zinn, the adequacy of state protection must be assessed in each case based on the facts, circumstances and country documentation presented to the decision-maker.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds RAD properly analyzed Applicants' circumstances, noting panels need not follow others and adequacy of protection is case-specific.

propositions.text: Application for judicial review will be dismissed
propositions.quote: The application will be dismissed.

paragraphs.summary: The court dismisses the application for judicial review.

propositions.text: Judgment: application dismissed and no question of general importance certified
propositions.quote: THIS COURT’S JUDGMENT is that: 1. The application for judicial review is dismissed. 2. No question of general importance is certified.

paragraphs.summary: Court orders dismissal of application and no certification of question of general importance.
